trust_decision.summary: Admin-uploaded SAML IdP metadata (file or URL) is parsed by a default JAXP DocumentBuilderFactory with DTDs/external entities enabled, to read entityID; nothing decides the XML is trusted, so external entities are resolved.

landing_point.why: Only raw JAXP parser factory in the GUI's SAML package; a grep for DocumentBuilderFactory lands here directly.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /api/samlconfig (SamlConfigController.create) and PATCH /api/samlconfig/{uuid} (update), via validateCreateProvider:76 / validateUpdateProvider:117

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The metadata-provider parse path (DbMetadataProvider/UrlMetadataProvider via OpenSAML StaticBasicParserPool) is library code a solver can argue is already hardened by OpenSAML defaults.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Valid IdP metadata (from file upload or URL) must still parse and yield entityID so create/update succeed; a fix that rejects all URL metadata or all namespaced XML would break provider registration.

O6_input_shapes: metadata fetched from admin-supplied URL (new URL(url).openStream)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Stored FILE metadata blob re-parsed by OpenSAML ParserPool when the provider is loaded/refreshed (DbMetadataProvider.fetchMetadata -> StaticBasicParserPool); hardening depends on xmltooling defaults, not on project code
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Parsing is done by OpenSAML's ParserPool, which a solver can argue is secure by default and outside the reported validator.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Configure StaticBasicParserPool with explicit builder features / a custom DocumentBuilderFactory that re-enables DTD loading (e.g. to support DOCTYPE-bearing IdP metadata)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Maintainers commonly tweak ParserPool features when some IdP metadata fails to parse; the bean is already declared here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A pre-parse of the stored blob with a plain DocumentBuilderFactory to check entityID before returning bytes
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Mirrors the existing validator helper; a reload-time sanity check is plausible in a provider that already queries the DB.
